cascade_hunts.title: KDS bump cascade: PREPARING → PREPARED end-to-end (single chef, happy path)
cascade_hunts.evidence: All 11 steps in scenario_K2_1 verified. Triple defense: (1) X-Idempotency-Key (replay safe), (2) expected_status optimistic-lock token in the FormRequest (concurrent stale UI rejected with 409), (3) DB::transaction + lockForUpdate row-level serialization. The KDS endpoint is STRUCTURALLY incapable of driving past PREPARED (FormRequest enum + KitchenReleaseRule.canTransition both gate). OrderStatusChanged broadcast is DispatchableAfterCommit safe — fires synchronously here only because dispatch site sits OUTSIDE the transaction closure (line 322 vs closure closes at 309).

cascade_hunts.title: POS Livré cascade: PREPARED → DELIVERED end-to-end (single cashier, happy path)
cascade_hunts.verdict: VERIFIED CITED — but uses different concurrency primitive than KDS path
cascade_hunts.evidence: All 9 steps in scenario_K2_2 verified. OrderService::changeStatus wraps the work in DB::transaction but does NOT call lockForUpdate on the route-bound model. The idempotent early-return at line 1941-1943 reads the IN-MEMORY $order copy. This is acceptable for the SINGLE-cashier path (HTTP X-Idempotency-Key + minute_bucket collapse double-tap to a Phase-1 replay) but does not protect against TWO cashiers in two browser sessions (see K2-H5). Compare with the KDS service path which explicitly acquires lockForUpdate at line 258-261.

cascade_hunts.title: Multi-bump race — chef bumps 3 orders within 500ms
cascade_hunts.evidence: Three orders bumped in rapid succession touch THREE DIFFERENT order rows. Each POST acquires its own row-level lockForUpdate in its own DB::transaction (KitchenDisplaySystemOrderService.php:258-261). No contention because no two writes target the same row. Throttle ceiling at kds-bump RateLimiter (RouteServiceProvider.php:193-196) = 120/min = 2/s — 3 bumps in 500ms (6/s instantaneous rate, but only 3 hits in the bucket window) ≪ 120/min ceiling. audit_logs HMAC chain extension for status transitions sits in OrderStatusTransition table writes (NOT audit_logs — that's NF525 cash-trail) so no chain bottleneck. KDS UI debounceRefresh at KitchenDisplaySystemComponent.vue:2182 collapses 3 burst refreshes into one (300ms). No UI freeze risk.

cascade_hunts.title: Bump-undo (recall) cascade — chef accidentally bumps wrong item
cascade_hunts.verdict: VERIFIED CITED — CLIENT-LOCAL ONLY, NO BACKEND TRANSITION REVERSAL
cascade_hunts.evidence: kdsRecall at KitchenDisplaySystemComponent.vue:1789-1797 dispatches kds/recallItem store action. Store action at kds.js:66-85 simply removes the per-item bumped timestamp from localStorage with a 60-second grace window (returns { ok: false, reason: 'grace_expired' } after 60s elapsed). NO BACKEND CALL. NO PATCH /api/admin/kds-order/change-status with status PREPARING (reverse transition). The recall ONLY un-marks the local item display state — if all items were previously bumped and triggered orderStatus(order, PREPARED), recalling one item does NOT trigger an inverse PREPARED→PREPARING server call (canTransition at KitchenReleaseRule:42-49 only allows forward edges + same-state idempotent, no reverse). So the recall UX gives the chef a 60s window to UN-MARK an item display flag but the order has ALREADY transitioned to PREPARED on the backend if all items were bumped; the recall does not un-deliver-PREPARED. This is intentional V1 behavior (revert is V1.0.2 backlog per Wave X3 LOCK_OrderStateMachine doc) but the UX could mislead a chef into thinking the recall reverses the server state when it does not.
cascade_hunts.remediation_suggestion: Either (a) DOCUMENT the V1 UX contract explicitly in the kds_bump_local_only_notice tooltip — already shown at line 121 + 1157 in KitchenDisplaySystemComponent.vue (so partial credit, but tooltip wording is generic 'local only' not 'cannot un-PREPARE') ; or (b) DISABLE the recall affordance entirely once isReadyOrder transitions the order to PREPARED so the affordance is consistent with what it can actually do; OR (c) V1.0.2 implement the reverse transition via a NEW dedicated endpoint with audit-trail + permission gate (per Wave X3 backlog). Owner-decision required.

cascade_hunts.title: Multi-cashier Livré race — 2 cashiers see same PREPARED order, both click Livré simultaneously
cascade_hunts.verdict: RED — AUDIT-TRAIL DUPLICATION + 2 BROADCASTS (data not corrupt but transition log polluted)
cascade_hunts.evidence: Per-row _delivering guard at PosComponent.vue:3108-3109 is CLIENT-LOCAL — does NOT serialize across cashier sessions. Backend ordering: (1) Cashier A clicks → posOrder/changeStatus → X-Idempotency-Key = sha(orderId + status payload + minute_bucket + USER_A) → middleware acquires scoped key. (2) Cashier B clicks within seconds → DIFFERENT scoped idempotency key (different userId per H2-HEAL-01 user_id scope) → middleware passes through. (3) Both controllers enter OrderService::changeStatus !$auth branch. (4) Both DB::transactions begin SIMULTANEOUSLY. (5) NO lockForUpdate on the bound $order — both read from the in-memory $order->status copy fetched OUTSIDE the transaction at route-resolve time. (6) The idempotent early-return at line 1941 (`if ((int) $order->status === $toStatus) return;`) sees $order->status === PREPARED (8) ≠ DELIVERED (11) for BOTH closures → both pass through. (7) Both write $order->status = DELIVERED + $order->save(). (8) Both call recordTransition(PREPARED, DELIVERED) at line 1998-2005 → 2 rows in order_status_transitions table for the SAME edge. (9) Both write ActionLog::create at line 2007-2017 → 2 audit rows in action_logs. (10) Both dispatch OrderStatusChanged at line 2055 → 2 broadcasts → 2 outbox rows (BUT PersistOrderStatusChangedToOutbox at line 27-33 sha1 idempotency_key includes correlation_id from X-Correlation-ID header; if both requests carry different correlation_ids — typical — then BOTH outbox rows survive firstOrCreate → 2 broadcast jobs → POS Q10 + OSS double-refresh, harmless cosmetic flicker). NET: order.status correctly = DELIVERED (idempotent target), no fiscal_sequence_no advance (DELIVERED is not a NF525 trigger), no audit_logs HMAC chain entry duplication (line 2020 limits NF525 chain to CANCELED/REJECTED/RETURNED). BUT: 2 OrderStatusTransition rows + 2 ActionLog rows pollute the operational audit trail; the QUI a livré question now has two answers. Cashier B sees the same success toast as Cashier A → 'I delivered this order' (false claim, B did not actually push the row to a customer). Cash drawer is NOT opened by Livré (cash is collected at Encaisser, not Livré) so no till-count risk like the H9 J-CASCADE finding.
cascade_hunts.remediation_suggestion: Add Order::query()->whereKey($order->id)->lockForUpdate()->firstOrFail() at the head of the DB::transaction closure in OrderService::changeStatus !$auth branch (line 1930-2043). Then re-check $locked->status === $targetStatus inside the closure (true idempotent guard against concurrent transitions). Cashier B then short-circuits inside the lock with the post-state of cashier A and returns the same OrderDetailsResource (already-DELIVERED) WITHOUT writing a second transition/ActionLog row. Optionally surface a flag in the response payload (already_delivered_by_other: true, user_id: X) so cashier B's toast can read 'Déjà marqué livré par {name}' instead of the generic success toast — owner-decision on UX wording. Mirrors KitchenDisplaySystemOrderService.php:258-261 pattern + OrderStateMachine::apply() pattern already in place (lines 208-253 of OrderStateMachine.php). The PaymentService::confirmCounterPayment at PaymentService.php:220-223 also already uses this pattern. The OrderService::changeStatus !$auth branch is the OUTLIER.

cascade_hunts.title: Echo subscription health — POS + KDS + OSS authenticated paths
cascade_hunts.verdict: VERIFIED CITED — POS has polling fallback, KDS has interceptor heal, OSS authenticated has Echo + ossSyncService
cascade_hunts.evidence: POS Echo at PosComponent.vue:2637-2696 wrapped in try/catch — silent fail logs nothing but polling fallback _kioskPollingInterval at :2602-2616 forces ≤5s cadence when readyOrders empty (per H-SYNC-001 / C2 from J-CASCADE H2). KDS Echo subscribeEcho() at KitchenDisplaySystemComponent.vue:1435 + axios response interceptor at :1448-1471 self-heals: any 2xx POST to admin/kds-order/change-status/* triggers immediate _refreshWithCurrentFilter + items() refresh regardless of Echo state. Plus kdsSyncService adaptive poller at :1478-1494 ticks on WS state change. OSS authenticated wall at PreparingAndReadyComponent.vue:257-289 wraps subscribeEcho in try/catch — silent fail console.warns but ossSyncService keeps polling. Triple-defense is sound on authenticated surfaces.

cascade_hunts.title: Long-poll vs WebSocket fallback — OSS public wall behavior when Soketi down
cascade_hunts.verdict: AMBER — WORST-CASE 60s LAG ON PUBLIC WALL (no Echo, only polling, cadence stays at 60s when WS reports connected)
cascade_hunts.evidence: OSS public TV wall (unauthenticated /admin/order-status-screen mounted with authBranchId=0) early-returns from subscribeEcho at PreparingAndReadyComponent.vue:260 — NO Echo subscription. Refresh is driven ENTIRELY by ossSyncService polling. ossSyncService cadence at OssSyncService.js:8-19: intervalMsWhenConnected=60000 (60s), intervalMsWhenDisconnected=2000 (2s), backoffStartMs=5000, backoffCapMs=30000. _wsState comes from window._wsService.on('connected'/'disconnected') at :138-189 — bound to the same Pusher socket but evaluated INDEPENDENTLY of OSS Echo subscription. So the public wall MAY report 'connected' (Soketi up, generic broadcasting auth open) → polls every 60s → chef bumps PREPARING→PREPARED at t=0 → customer wall sees the order in PRÊT column up to ~60s late. If Soketi is DOWN (or _wsService never reaches connected) → 2s polling → worst-case ~2s lag (acceptable). Burst-poll on visibilitychange at :214-226 collapses lag when operator brings tab forward, but the public wall NEVER receives visibility events (TV is always visible). NET: in the most common deployment (Soketi up + public wall) the customer-facing lag is the WORST it can be in this system (60s) — exact opposite of the operator-facing surfaces which get the BEST (Echo <1s).
cascade_hunts.remediation_suggestion: Either (a) wire a public broadcasting channel `public-branch.{id}` mounted via Echo with no auth (already explored for catalog availability — sister of `private-branch.{id}` for kiosk frontend) and have the OSS public wall subscribe to it; OR (b) tighten intervalMsWhenConnected for the PUBLIC wall surface only (e.g. detect authBranchId===0 in startOssSync and override to 5000ms) — owner-decision; tradeoff is HTTP load on the OSS endpoint (each wall = 12/min vs 1/min currently); OR (c) accept the 60s lag and document it in the operations runbook. Note: the current design assumes the kitchen calls out the order verbally to the customer when they bump, so the wall is reinforcement not primary signal — owner mandate.

data_integrity_attestation.kds_bump_path: INTACT — KitchenDisplaySystemOrderService uses lockForUpdate + expected_status optimistic-lock + idempotent early-return triple defense. Multi-bump race safe by design (different rows = no contention). FormRequest enum gate makes structurally impossible to drive past PREPARED via KDS.
data_integrity_attestation.pos_livre_path: DEGRADED — OrderService::changeStatus !$auth branch lacks lockForUpdate inside its DB::transaction. Multi-cashier race produces duplicate OrderStatusTransition + ActionLog rows for the same PREPARED→DELIVERED edge. Order.status correctly converges to DELIVERED (idempotent target), but operational audit trail is polluted. No NF525 chain impact (DELIVERED is not a fiscal trigger).
data_integrity_attestation.oss_public_wall: DEGRADED LATENCY — no Echo subscription on the unauthenticated wall surface; relies on 60s polling cadence when WS reports connected. Up to 60s lag between chef bump and customer-visible state on the TV.
data_integrity_attestation.broadcast_outbox: INTACT — PersistOrderStatusChangedToOutbox idempotency_key includes correlation_id so duplicate listener fires within the same request collapse; cross-request duplicate transitions (K2-H5) get separate outbox rows (acceptable — both broadcast jobs are no-op on the receivers because order.status already DELIVERED). DB::afterCommit dispatch guarantees no broadcast on rollback. WJ-4 OBS-OUTBOX-01 hardening logs Pusher failures + dispatches OutboxBroadcastSwallowedEvent for alerting.

race_conditions_identified.scenario: K2-H3 — Chef bumps 3 orders within 500ms (different order rows)
race_conditions_identified.outcome: Safe by design. Each row acquires its own lockForUpdate in its own DB::transaction. Throttle ceiling 120/min not threatened. Debounced refresh on KDS UI collapses to one re-render.

ux_friction_points.where: OSS public wall — chef bumps PREPARING→PREPARED → customer sees Prêt up to 60s late
ux_friction_points.issue: Public wall has no Echo subscription (auth gate); ossSyncService polls every 60s when WS reports connected. Customer waiting at counter for their order number to light up may walk away or harass cashier asking 'is my order ready?'.
Two cashiers can independently click Livré on same order, both see success toast, audit trail says both delivered. No 'this was already delivered by {other_cashier}' feedback.
ux_friction_points.fix_size: ~20 lines (lockForUpdate + post-state response flag + modal toast branch)

ux_friction_points.where: KDS recall affordance — visible AFTER order has transitioned to PREPARED
ux_friction_points.issue: kdsRecall un-marks the local item bump display, but does NOT trigger backend PREPARED→PREPARING reverse transition (canTransition does not allow it). Chef may think recall un-prepares the order; downstream POS Q10 still sees order as PREPARED.
ux_friction_points.fix_size: ~5 lines (template v-if guard hides recall when order.status === PREPARED) OR ~80 lines (V1.0.2 backend reverse-transition endpoint with audit + permission)

verdict_rationale: Cascade is functionally correct for the happy paths. KDS bump path is hardened (triple defense via FormRequest enum + lockForUpdate + expected_status token + KitchenReleaseRule structural gate). POS Livré path is correct for single-cashier use case but lacks lockForUpdate inside the closure → multi-cashier race produces duplicate operational audit rows (NOT data corruption, NOT NF525 chain pollution, NOT till-count risk — cash drawer is opened at Encaisser not at Livré). OSS public TV wall has a 60s worst-case lag between chef bump and customer-visible PREPARED state — acceptable per owner mandate (kitchen calls out orders verbally, wall is reinforcement) but worth documenting. Three discrete findings: K2-H5 multi-cashier Livré race (P1), K2-H7 public wall 60s lag (P2), K2-H4 KDS recall UX confusion (P2). No P0 findings. Ship-ready for V1 Le Cayenne single-cashier use case with owner-decision needed on K2-H5 for V1.0.1 hardening.
top_5_cascade_concerns: K2-H5 (P1) — Multi-cashier Livré race: 2 cashiers can both click Livré on same PREPARED order; both succeed; 2 OrderStatusTransition + 2 ActionLog rows; ambiguous 'who delivered' attribution. Add lockForUpdate inside OrderService::changeStatus !$auth DB::transaction (OrderService.php:1930).

K2-H7 (P2) — OSS public TV wall worst-case 60s lag between chef bump and customer-visible PREPARED state. No Echo subscription on authBranchId=0 surface; ossSyncService polls every 60s when WS reports connected. Acceptable per owner mandate but worth wiring public-branch.{id} channel or tightening cadence to 5s for authBranchId=0.

K2-H4 (P2) — KDS recall affordance is local-only; UX may mislead chef into thinking reverse PREPARED→PREPARING transition fires. Either tighten tooltip wording or hide affordance when order.status === PREPARED.

K2-H6 (INFO) — Echo subscription health on operator-attended surfaces (POS + KDS + OSS authenticated) is well-defended (try/catch + polling fallback + KDS axios interceptor self-heal). No silent-fail risk.
